objections.claim: The ratchet compares raw working-tree bytes (`fs.statSync(p).size`, no normalisation) against a baseline committed from one checkout. This makes the entire CI gate hostage to an environmental invariant the spec asserts but does not secure: that every checkout and CI runner materialises identical bytes. §6 notes only "no `.gitattributes` today" — but the moment anyone adds eol normalisation (a common repo hygiene change, often unrelated to faff), or a Windows contributor with `core.autocrlf=true` runs locally, every one of the 41 covered files mismatches its baseline simultaneously and the gate reds with 41 spurious FAILs that no `--lower` call can fix (the files did not shrink; the checkout changed).
objections.evidence: §3 Vocabulary ("bytes … with no normalisation"), §4.4 "CRLF or BOM. Bytes are counted raw", §6 "This holds while the repo has no `.gitattributes` … the repo has no `.gitattributes` today". The spec treats eol drift as a *correct* signal ("a line-ending change shows as growth or shrink, which is correct") — true for an intentional edit, false for an environmental conversion touching all 41 files at once, which the design cannot distinguish.
objections.predicted_consequence: the first `.gitattributes` introduction (or an autocrlf contributor) turns the gate permanently red or forces a whole-file baseline rewrite that masks real drift; the fix is a one-line spec edit (pin `* -text` for the covered set, or state the invariant as a guarded assumption with a doctor/CI check).
objections.disposition_rationale: A new .gitattributes marks the covered set -text, so checkouts cannot convert line endings (spec §4.2, DONE item added).

objections.claim: The slice lands a zero-headroom byte baseline over all 41 covered files while two open PRs (#1169 FAFF-1436, #1170 FAFF-1444) already edit `SKILL.md` files. Whichever merges after this one cannot pass CI without a baseline edit on rebase — a hard sequencing coupling the critique surfaces as a "sequencing note" but the spec never elevates to a dependency or a mitigation (e.g. land this after both, or pre-agree the rebase step with those PR owners).
objections.evidence: Methodology critique: "Open PRs #1169 (FAFF-1436) and #1170 (FAFF-1444) both edit `SKILL.md` files and will need a one-line baseline update on rebase." Spec §4.4: "Parallel PRs after this lands… whichever merges after this one rebases and runs `--lower` or a hand raise."
objections.predicted_consequence: One of the two open PRs fails `validate-adapters` on rebase with a `prose bytes` FAIL its author did not plan for, producing either an unplanned mid-review baseline edit or a blocked PR until someone runs `--lower`.
objections.disposition_rationale: §4.2 sequences this graft after PRs #1169 and #1170 merge; both have merged.

objections.claim: §4.5's instruction for testing the absent-baseline FAIL ("run against a temp copy of the skills dir, never by touching the real file") contradicts the interface table: with `--skills-dir` given and the baseline absent, the specified behaviour is an INFO skip, not a FAIL. The FAIL-missing branch is reachable only via the default skills-dir resolution, which is script-relative to the real binary — so a tester following the spec's named route observes INFO + exit 0 where the DONE item ("fails when prose-baseline.json is missing") expects exit 1.
objections.evidence: §4.5 bullet "The bundled tree with the baseline file moved aside fails `missing` (run against a temp copy of the skills dir, never by touching the real file)"; interface row "baseline file absent, `--skills-dir` given → INFO … none"; DONE "faff validate-adapters with no --skills-dir fails when prose-baseline.json is missing or malformed".
objections.predicted_consequence: the DONE item's test, built exactly as the spec describes, passes vacuously (it exercises the INFO-skip branch) while the FAIL-missing branch ships untested — or a builder "fixes" the test by touching the real file, which the spec forbids.
objections.disposition_rationale: §4.5 runs a copied binary with no --skills-dir so the script-relative default resolves to the copy and exercises the missing-baseline FAIL.
